definition: A device that uses the turning effect on a current-carrying coil between the poles of a magnet to spin an axle; more turns on the coil, a bigger current or a stronger magnetic field give a bigger turning effect.

A metal ring cut into two insulated halves on the axle of a d.c. motor, one joined to each end of the coil, that reverses the current in the coil every half turn so the coil keeps turning in one direction.
